first_mistake.description: Searches found no travel-notification procedure, but the agent presented invented instructions (app menu path, a 1-800-RHO-BANK phone number) as 'according to our documentation' instead of admitting the KB has no information. That removed the path in which the customer asks for a transfer (kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer).

detectable_without_answer_key.signal: Specific procedural content (phone number, menu path, lead-time advice) in an agent message that appears in no retrieved tool output; the KB searches returned no travel-notification procedure.

notes: This is fabricated guidance rather than a wrong tool action. The transfer-reason-code doc (042) was never retrieved, but the no-fabrication rule is general, so rule_available_before is null.

first_mistake.description: Same pattern as the other task_012 run. With no KB procedure found (only 'enable travel notifications' mentions), the agent gave invented steps and a phone number. It never said the information was missing, so the customer never asked for the expected transfer.

detectable_without_answer_key.signal: Agent message states app navigation and a phone number not present in any retrieved document; greps for travel notification returned only passing mentions.

notes: At [35] it partly admitted 'the KB does not list an exact menu label', but it still gave detailed invented steps, and the customer ended satisfied.

first_mistake.description: Identity verification failed: the email didn't match and the customer couldn't give a second field. The agent then transferred with reason customer_requests_human_no_specific_reason. The Tier-1 code account_ownership_dispute covers identity verification failures and takes priority.

detectable_without_answer_key.signal: A transfer_to_human_agents call made with no retrieval of the transfer reason-code doc, after a failed lookup by the customer-supplied email and only 1 of 2 verification fields matched; a rule could map 'verification incomplete' to the expected code.

notes: Everything else was handled appropriately (it refused to change the email without verification). Only the reason code was wrong.

first_mistake.description: For the Business Gold Rewards Card, the agent gave the get_referral_link tool without retrieving that card's referral document, which says the program stopped accepting referrals on 2025-09-15. It falsely told the customer it had found the program in the KB. Its grep for 'referral' was truncated before the Business Gold doc.

detectable_without_answer_key.signal: give_discoverable_user_tool(get_referral_link) for a card_name with no retrieved referral-program document for that card, even though the already-retrieved doc_009 pre-check requires confirming one.

notes: The underlying violation is timing (an expired program). It is classed RETRIEVAL because the expiry rule was never in context. At [14] it offered a human transfer, which doc_009 forbids in this case, but never made one.

first_mistake.description: The agent read the Business Gold referral doc ('accepts new referrals until 2025-09-15') and still gave get_referral_link for that card, after an earlier call with a malformed tool name failed at [22]. It even repeated the expired deadline to the customer. The program had already closed.

detectable_without_answer_key.signal: A retrieved document's end date (2025-09-15) is earlier than the session date; comparing dates against get_current_time would flag the tool hand-off. The agent never called get_current_time.

notes: i=24 is the first successful hand-off; the attempt at [22] errored. The current date was never fetched, so evidence_available_before is null. At [16] it offered a transfer contrary to doc_009 but did not perform one.

It then chose the no-account option and ended. Without an identifier the agent could not look up the account or give the cash-back dispute tool.

detectable_without_answer_key.signal: The customer declines every lookup identifier the agent asks for, and the conversation ends with no user lookup or log_verification.

notes: Hard to classify. The agent said it had no phone/DOB lookup tool; if one existed this would be TOOL_ACCESS, which I can't confirm from permitted files. It also cited a 'Points Rounding Policy' that never appears in visible retrievals.

Elite tier gets RUSH shipping and PREMIUM design at $0, and the customer had asked for 'the best option that's free with my account'. At [103] it also ordered the Light Green (Entry-tier) replacement immediately, breaking the 48-hour wait after closure.

detectable_without_answer_key.signal: order_debit_card_5739 called while the tier replacement policy doc was never read; for Light Green, an order issued minutes after a close_debit_card_4721 receipt on the same account.

notes: Contested because the customer explicitly accepted 'standard and classic' after the agent framed them as the free defaults. The TIMING breach at [103] is a second independent failure.

first_mistake.description: In one turn the agent fired two close_debit_card calls (both failed, the cards were FROZEN) and an order_debit_card for Bluest with STANDARD/CLASSIC. It had retrieved doc 029 and told the customer Elite shipping is complimentary, and the customer asked for the best free option (RUSH/PREMIUM). detectable_without_answer_key.signal: An order_debit_card_5739 receipt in the same turn as failed close_debit_card_4721 calls (order before successful closure); delivery_option STANDARD although the retrieved tier doc lists $0 RUSH for Elite and the customer requested the best free option.

notes: At [92] it ordered the Light Green replacement right after closure, despite having told the customer about the 48-hour wait. At [94] it falsely said the order was 'placed after closure and 48-hour wait was respected' (a receipt exists, so I didn't count it as an unbacked CLAIM).

first_mistake.description: Instead of giving the customer submit_cash_back_dispute_0589 (doc_003), the agent changed rewards directly with update_transaction_rewards_3847. Per doc_004 that tool is only for resolved disputes. Neither doc was ever retrieved. It also added +1 point to two transactions that were correctly truncated.

detectable_without_answer_key.signal: update_transaction_rewards_3847 called with no cash-back dispute record looked up and no retrieved document authorizing direct correction; reward edits applied to the customer's own disputed transactions in the same session.

notes: Earlier, at [49], it restricted the review to self-defined 'closed cycles' (borrowed from the Platinum rebate window doc), finding only 1 of the 4 expected discrepant transactions. [63] claims it 'opened a consolidated rewards review' and 'logged case', with no tool receipt for either.

first_mistake.description: The agent applied a $100 interest correction and reported expected APY 6.875%. It added the Gold Rewards Card +0.025% (called a 'relationship bonus' in doc 013) on top of the EcoCard +0.6%, but doc 014/045 treat it as a credit-card bonus that does not stack. The expected figures were 6.85% and $98.

detectable_without_answer_key.signal: Recompute APY components from the retrieved docs (base + highest checking boost + highest credit-card bonus) and compare to the credit amount. The doc 013 'relationship bonus' wording makes a deterministic rule ambiguous.

notes: Doc 013's wording supports the agent's stacking, so this is contested. Later the agent transferred (specialized_department_required) for a 12-month 'archived history' review, even though the history showed a single interest posting.

The task's ground truth is that the customer qualifies (Diamond Elite application expected). The customer then applied for the Silver Rewards Card.

notes: Hard to verify: the stored transcript truncates the 60-transaction tool output, so I can't confirm whether the error was arithmetic, an exclusion, or window assignment (TIMING).
